display_name: Shafer Vineyards One Point Five, Napa Valley
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Shafer One Point Five Cabernet Sauvignon sources from younger estate vines in Stags Leap District, where gravelly alluvial soils and cooling marine fog produce Napa reds with blackcurrant depth and restrained power. This 100% Cab hits 15.3% ABV in recent vintages, balancing ripeness with structure. Limited critic medals from TEXSOM highlight its consistent appeal.",
  "wine_summary": "Shafer Vineyards, family-owned since 1973, farms 50 hillside acres in Stags Leap District, prioritizing estate fruit over purchased grapes—a rarity in Napa where blending is common. One Point Five serves as their accessible Cabernet, from younger vines than the flagship Hillside Select, yet it carries the estate's signature polish. In Napa Valley's 122,735 acres of alluvial and volcanic soils, Shafer's site on the alluvial fans delivers wines that age globally competitive, as proven in the 1976 Judgment of Paris where a Shafer relative shone.",
  "terroir_expression": "Gravelly alluvial soils in Stags Leap District, part of Napa's valley floor deposits like Bale loam, drain fast to stress vines and build grippy tannins, while diurnal swings from San Pablo Bay fog temper alcohol and preserve blackcurrant cassis and graphite notes. This setup yields darker cherry and cedar over green pepper pyrazines common in cooler Cab zones, with iron-rich streaks adding tobacco persistence. Hillside proximity infuses subtle volcanic minerality, tightening the mid-palate.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested estate fruit ferments in small lots, often with native yeasts to layer complexity, then ages 20 months in French oak—mostly new for structure without oak dominance. Pump-overs extract color and tannins gently, preserving fruit purity; rackings clarify without fining. This approach, rooted in Shafer's sustainable farming, concentrates flavors from low-yield vines, explaining the wine's firm yet integrated frame.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled ribeye steak with chimichurri: tannins grip the fat, cassis echoes beef juices, acidity cuts char. Nashville hot chicken: heat amplifies black pepper notes, fruit cools spice without clashing. Beef Wellington: pastry richness meets cedar depth, plum acidity slices through duxelles. Lamb shank braised in red wine: earthiness matches graphite, structure holds braise intensity. Cheeseburger with aged cheddar: casual melt pairs with dark chocolate hints, tannins firm the bite.",
  "comparable_wines": "Spottswoode Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley — similar Stags Leap alluvial gravel yields cassis-driven structure at $150+. Silver Oak Alexander Valley Cabernet — Alexander Valley warmth mirrors Napa ripeness, softer tannins for $140 range. Chappellet Signature Cabernet — eastern Napa sedimentary soils deliver comparable graphite and aging curve around $130.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry Cabernet with grippy tannins and blackcurrant persistence",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink from 2026-2037 for 2022 vintage as tannins integrate. Store at 55°F, 70% humidity, on side to keep corks moist.",
  "value_assessment": "$127-$140 retail. Caymus Napa Cabernet and Opus One second wine compete here. Buy for superior structure and aging over fruit-forward rivals—estate purity justifies the spend.",
  "market_position": "Napa loyalists and steakhouse somms stock this for by-the-glass programs. Collectors pair it with Hillside Select in cellars. Retail at high-end shops like Wally's moves it to trade-up buyers from $80 Cabs.",
  "insider_take": "Most chase Napa fruit bombs, missing One Point Five's restrained power that builds over a decade. Tradeoff is early firmness for graphite evolution. Buy if you cellar; skip for instant gratification.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 4,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,

  }
}
